myths.title: Name and Meaning
myths.text: The name means "The Man-Lion — the fourth avatāra of Viṣṇu" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition.

lore.syncretism: Narasiṃha appears within the Sanskrit tradition and has influenced later retellings, artistic depictions, and scholarly study. The Unicode restoration preserves the name's distinctive orthography for contemporary use.
lore.culturalLegacy: Narasiṃha continues to appear in scholarship, art, and popular reception as a significant figure of the Sanskrit tradition. Restoring the name in Unicode returns the original marks that ASCII removes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Narasiṃha embodies man-lion avatar in the Sanskrit imagination. The name's restoration is not merely cosmetic: it recovers the stress, length, and script that make the figure recognizable in the source tradition.
lore.archaeology: Narasiṃha is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Sanskrit tradition.
